elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 permits Ono to terminate “at any time during the Term” and “for any reason,” including in whole.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires thirty (30) days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly requires “thirty (30) days' advance” notice.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly requires “written notice to Array.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Array must refund Ono “any amounts prepaid by Ono in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination,” which provides the required time-based pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language grants only Ono a without-cause right. The referenced Array termination rights concern Ono's breach or prohibited Competing Product activity, not convenience termination.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Ono may terminate “at any time during the Term” and “for any reason.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; therefore, there is no fee exceeding the permitted cap.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted in the supplied operative language, so Vendor cannot exercise such a right before the end of a term.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted, so the condition triggering this notice requirement is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline satisfies every preferred element: Ono receives an throughout-the-Term convenience right on 30 days' written notice, with a refund of prepaid amounts attributable to the post-termination period, and Array receives no corresponding convenience right. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because 30 days is not within the required 60–90-day range. The redline is not minimal because it additionally permits Product-by-Product and country-by-country termination, which was not required. It also fails to cleanly preserve the preexisting rationale requirement: placing “which shall be accompanied by the rationale” after the new refund clause creates ambiguity about what must be accompanied by the rationale and potentially changes or obscures the original notice obligation.
